name: Kwakiutl

ancestors.notes: Descent per Glottolog classification of Kwak'wala (kwak1269).

notes: Research. Northern Wakashan language of northern Vancouver Island and the adjacent British Columbia coast, written in the practical orthography promoted by the Uʼmista Cultural Society (the wikipron/wiktionary gold this spec is scored against uses that alphabet, confirmed against the School District 85 Kwakʼwala IRP 2010 alphabet poster cited by Wikipedia's Kwakʼwala article: the underline diacritic on a/g/x marks schwa and the uvular series, the raised comma marks ejectives, and Dł/dł and Ł/ł are the lateral obstruents). The gold also mixes in variant community/NAPA spellings of the same phonemes -- c/ƛ/ǧ/x̌/ḵ alongside dz-ts/dł-ł/g̱-x̱ -- so both spellings are mapped where they resolve to the same sound. Ejectives (raised comma above, U+0313, postposed on obstruents c/k/p/q/t/ƛ and on the labialized/uvular clusters; preposed apostrophe on the sonorants w/y/l/m/n) and the uvular uderline series (g̱=ɢ, x̱=χ, ḵ=q) are now mapped with a per-value citation to the Uʼmista alphabet table; affricates ts/dz/tł/dł/ƛ carry the IPA tie bar (U+0361), matching this project's convention elsewhere (see e.g. ewo.json) and the phonemic value given for the letter in the Uʼmista chart -- some individual wikipron word-level entries transcribe dł/Ꟛ without an affricate (as [d͡l] rather than [d͡ɮ]), which is a gold-internal inconsistency (letter-name entries use the phonemic value, running-word entries a looser one) documented in the PR, not chased. Kwakʼwala's lambda-with-stroke ƛ/Ƛ (voiceless lateral affricate) and lambda ꟛ/Ꟛ (voiced lateral affricate) are the dedicated Unicode Latin Extended-D letters for Wakashan/Salishan orthographies (U+019B/U+A7DC and U+A7DB/U+A7DA respectively). Grapheme table checked against Boas (1947): no discrepancy found for the base (non-ejective, non-uvular) series. GOLD COMPOSITION: of the 116 wikipron/kwk gold entries, 108 are single-letter or grapheme-chart rows (e.g. "Q" -> [q], "Łw" -> [ɬʷ]) and only 8 are real running words; PER on the chart subset is 0.0 (trivially perfect, since it is scoring the letter table against itself) and PER on the 8 real-word subset is 0.1009. The board's headline 0.007 is therefore essentially alphabet recitation, not a measurement of running-text accuracy, and the 0.1009 figure is itself only a sample of 8 words -- far too small to serve as a benchmark on its own. STRESS EXEMPTION: Boas (1947) and later work (Bach 1975; Elfner 2024) describe Kwakʼwala prominence as quantity-sensitive (heavy syllables -- non-schwa vowels closed by a sonorant coda, or bimoraic vowels -- attract stress) and, in current analyses, assigned at the phrase level rather than as a fixed word-position rule; this is not a function this project's positional `stress` schema can express without a syllable-weight primitive keyed to the mora, so no `stress` block is added rather than encoding a wrong approximation.
